items.heading: Here Is the Structural Fact
items.text: Here is the structural fact that separates dairy science from almost every other agri-food branch: the industry runs on two genuinely different employment systems at once, and a graduate's early-career experience depends almost entirely on which one they enter.

items.heading: "Dairy Technology" and "Dairy Science"
items.text: "Dairy technology" and "dairy science" get used almost interchangeably, but the admission routes into them genuinely differ, and the difference matters for how competitive your entry actually is.

rows: Fresher, cooperative dairy plant or district union (QA, production trainee)
A modest floor, but it comes with quasi-government job security and a structured, predictable progression rare in private FMCG.
Milk Procurement Officer, cooperative federation or district union
A genuinely dairy-specific role with no real private-sector equivalent, stable, but structurally capped by cooperative pay bands and dependent on real rural fieldwork.
Pay Level 6 (roughly ₹35,400-1,12,400 basic) plus allowances, gross typically ₹4.5-7 lakh/year
Government-structured pay bands with slow, predictable progression; recruitment runs through state PSCs on an irregular cycle, not every year.

items.heading: Most People Who Have Heard
items.text: Most people who have heard the phrase "dairy science" know it only through an Amul hoarding or a school trip to a milk collection centre, few realise it is a real B.Tech/B.Sc degree with its own flagship deemed university, NDRI Karnal, not a vague sub-topic inside agriculture.

items.heading: Families Assume the Entire Career
items.text: Families assume the entire career is "getting posted at Amul," as if Amul were one company with one HR desk that a graduate simply joins.

items.heading: Because the Field Sits Next
items.text: Because the field sits next to agriculture and veterinary science on a college brochure, it gets mentally filed as a low-paying, rural-only path with no real corporate ladder, the opposite of how food technology or biotechnology usually get framed.
